title: Evening Bridge Release Rituals and Observability Notes
content:
Context and intent:
This living scratchpad captures a lightweight 'evening bridge' ritual for small-scope rollouts and dark-launches that start late-afternoon and transition into overnight monitoring. Goal: reduce hit-or-miss handoffs, keep the night crew informed, and preserve a compact telemetry sampling plan so we don't overwhelm on-call.

Why a separate ritual?
- Many release docs are written for full-day launches. Night launches need a tighter, hour-by-hour sentinel and a clear minimal playbook (fast decisions, fewer actors).
- This doc intentionally biases for low-touch operations: smaller blast radius, short observation windows, pre-baked fallback lanes.

Quick summary (one-line):
Evening bridge = 3-step handoff (deploy verification -> 3-hr guarded observation -> automated throttle/fallback), plus a tiny telemetry sample and a short release-notes stub for followup.

Evening bridge checklist (to be completed before handoff):
- Deploy slot: confirm CI/CD job finished and artifacts are pinned (CI job: platform-release/nightly-flow #8421).
- Health smoke: run smoke suite (smoke: /ops/smoke/evening) -> all green.
- Canary fraction: set initial ramp to 0.5% for high-risk endpoints, 5% for low-risk.
- Telemetry taps: enable 1-min sampling on latency p50/p95 and error-rate for service groups: inference-proxy, tokenizer, batch-worker.
- Alert set: ensure alert mute window not covering this release (alerts referenced in RELE-4123) and create ephemeral alert rule: evening-bridge-ephemeral.
- Escalation contacts: primary engineer (owner), secondary on-call (SRE), release steward. Add chatroom: #bridge-RELE-4123.
- Ops knobs: pre-stage rollback job (one-click rollback tag: rollback/RELE-4123), traffic-shaper config, and a standby smaller model (model-v1-small) for fallback.

Hour-by-hour cadence (first 4 hours):
T+0 (deploy complete)
- Validate: basic health endpoints, 10 quick inference requests (sample prompts), core metrics p50/p95, error-rate. Explicit checklist: 5 passes of smoke.
- Post-deploy note: append to release-notes stub (below) with timestamp.

T+15m
- Confirm telemetry streams are flowing into dashboards (console -> route: /release/RELE-4123). Verify logs for sampling headers.
- If any errors >0.5% or p95 latency increased by >30%: throttle to previous config and call rollback decision.

T+60m
- Evaluate core signals (latency, errors, saturation). Run small traffic simulation (10 RPS for 5m) to observe tail effects.
- If signs of resource pressure (GPU memory growth, queueing): enable burst throttle and reduce concurrency. Tag incidents in the runbook.

T+180m (3 hours)
- Decision gate: continue to full ramp (move to production split per release plan) OR maintain extended guard OR execute rollback. Decision recorded in channel and runbook.

Observability and sampling plan (compact):
- Short window sampling only: 1-min aggregates for p50/p95, 10s sampling for error-counts for the first 60m then 5m aggregates after 90m.
- Logs: set verbose sampling only for a narrow request trace selector (trace header: X-Bridge-Sample). Capture first 30 traces of any 5xx.
- Traces: enable full spans on 'request-prepare' and 'kv-cache' paths for the first 30m.
- Synthetic checks: spin up 4 synthetics from the us-west and eu-west regions hitting the canonical prompt set (synth suite id: bridge-quick-1).

Decision lattice (how to escalate quickly):
- Signal: isolated 5xx bursts on one node -> action: remove node from pool, drain, reprovision. Owner: infra on-call.
- Signal: system-wide p95 latency +50% -> action: reduce concurrency, enable fallback model, notify release steward.
- Signal: slow error accumulation (errors rising slowly over 2 hours) -> action: pause ramp, increase sampling frequency, escalate to SRE.
- Signal: sudden traffic spike unrelated to release -> action: follow normal surge playbook (not covered here) but do not attribute to release without traces.

Rollback matrix (simple, binary lanes preferred for nights):
- Fast rollback (immediate): any sustained 5xx >1% for 5m OR p95 increased >2x baseline. Command: rollback/RELE-4123 tag.
- Gradual rollback (throttle down): resource pressure signs or progressive latency/regression in embeddings quality vs baseline. Action: reduce traffic to canary and follow up with perf team.

Communication templates (fill and send to channel):
- Short update (post at T+15): "RELE-4123: deploy complete, canary=0.5% (inference-proxy). Smoke: PASS. Telemetry streaming. Next check T+60. @oncall-sre on standby"
- Alert message (if action): "ALERT: RELE-4123 p95 latency +60% vs baseline over 5m. Throttling to safe config; rollback job ready. Paging @oncall-sre and release steward."

Release notes stub (capture at deploy, for product digest):
- Title: "RELE-4123: Incremental latency/kv-cache opt, small model fallback"
- Summary (one line): "Tightening platform KV cache eviction heuristics to reduce memory pressure during long-context sessions; introduces an automated small-model fallback to preserve latency SLAs."
- Impact: "Most customers: no visible change. High-long-context flows: reduced tail latency, small risk of transient 5xx during initial warmup."
- Rollout: "Canary 0.5% -> 3 hr observation -> ramp per schedule"
- Known issues: "Edge case: rare tokenization mismatch for legacy prompts; rollback tag prepared."
- Followups: "Add regression test for tokenizer edge case (ticket: RELE-4167)."

Post-release followups (to add after morning):
- Add detailed telemetry dump to confluence (template: /releases/RELE-4123/postmortem).
- If rollback occurred: fill the rollback incident form and tag impacted customers.
- Action items: ensure the ephemeral alert is removed and replaced with persistent one if needed.

Quick heuristics and notes to self (loose bullets):
- Prefer throttle over full rollback for marginal perf regressions in the night — keeps user-facing availability.
- Keep the initial canary tiny for model-serving changes that alter memory/kernels.
- Tag logs liberally during ramp; delete verbose logs later.
- If you are not sure: take the conservative option and hold the ramp. Night crews prefer fewer context switches.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the synthetic set (bridge-quick-1) representative of multi-turn production prompts? Looks lightweight; consider expanding to 10 prompts.
- Automate ephemeral alerts creation from a template (Jira: automations/alerts-template).
- Should we surface a one-click 'pause plateau' in the console? File UX ticket if morning team agrees.

Appendix: quick command cheats (not exhaustive):
- Rollback: ./bin/release rollback --tag rollback/RELE-4123
- Throttle: console route -> traffic-shaper -> set canary 0.5% -> 0.1% if needed
- Quick trace capture: curl -H "X-Bridge-Sample: 1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/text/complete -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

End of sketch — this is intentionally compact. Use as a one-page handoff for small evening launches; expand to full runbook if we adopt this pattern for more complex releases.

Notes: leaving some fragments for the next pass — Priya, Liam: please add any infra knobs I missed and tag the synthetic prompt set you prefer.
